text: The catalogue stays single and owned by P6 rwb-comms in rwb_comms; the P7 copy of the legacy key delivers the record side only. rwb-decision keeps one template_use row per accepted answer, naming the template code, language, version, catalog version in force, merge codes, notice type, product group, approver reference, valid from and business date, all resolved through RWB-P6-E1046-CON and never copied from a catalog table. The catalogue itself, its load, its version numbering, its approval, its withdrawal and its current-version selection stay RWB-P6-E1046-CON and RWB-P6-E1046-APP.
why: The FSD P7 module claims FEAT-DRI-16 and the story RWB-E1-046 while the Ownership Map and the context pack give template and merge_field to P6 and give P7 six other tables; a second catalogue in rwb_decision would breach DP-01 and would let two catalog versions drift.
read: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 feature table and A2.12; FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-010-01; TSD P7 v2 T3.1; Context pack P7 ownership rows; RWB-P6-E1046-CON sections 11 and 12.7; WP B2-P7-013 story line.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-comms and rwb-decision owners at the Service Contract Catalog review
impact: Medium: if the solution architect instead gives the catalogue to P7, the two P6 slices and the four RWB-ITG stories of the key are re-issued; no behaviour of this story changes.

text: The recorded reference lives in one table of rwb_decision named template_use, created by the migration V_E1046__template_use.sql in the per-service Flyway sequence, with the primary key id, the unique key (entry_ref, template_code, language), the index (template_code, language, business_date) and the columns entry_ref, template_code, language, template_version, catalog_version, merge_codes, notice_type, product_group, approver_ref, valid_from, business_date and state; the names and types are fixed by the rwb_decision DB story and carried as "template_use" until then.
why: No source names the row that holds the template reference, its columns or its migration; DP-01 and DP-15 still require it to be a table of this service's schema written by its own Flyway sequence, and the ACs cannot be asserted without a named shape.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (no template column on decision_log_entry); FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-010-01; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; RWB-P7-E1027-APP section 11 (the sibling default shape).
confirm: ACE DB owner and the rwb_decision DB story, before the rwb_decision baseline is created
impact: Low: a different table or column set touches one migration, one entity, one repository and one section of this story; the behaviour is unchanged.

text: The plan's dependency rows are followed as written: Depends on (build) is None, the contract dependency is RWB-P6-E1046-CON and there is no I or X row. The three H rows the DP table adds (RWB-PLT-E1043-CON for DP-07, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON for DP-15 and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for DP-19) are read as wave-0 platform prerequisites of the service template, the reference-data client and the edge, so lane L-P7-M and the Day-1 start do not change.
why: The plan and the DP table disagree on the H rows and a story cannot carry two dependency lists; the sibling slices of this same run follow the plan's list and treat the platform contracts as wave-0 prerequisites, which keeps the Day-1 rule of section R5.7 intact.
read: WP B2-P7-013 story line; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.4, R5.5 (DP-07, DP-15, DP-19) and R5.7; Context pack P7 service row.
confirm: Solution architect at the Service Contract Catalog review
impact: If the three become real build dependencies the lane waits for the wave-0 contract stories; the behaviour of the recorded row does not change.

text: The current version of a template code and language is read as GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates with the query parameters for the template code, the language, the state Approved and the business date, answering the version with its state, approver, approval date, valid from, notice type, channel and signature basis; the query and answer field names are agreed with the rwb-comms contract owner at the contract review and the story is built and tested against the fake until then.
why: RWB-P6-E1046-CON fixes the operation and the resource names, its field-level shapes are recorded there as unspecified and API Specification v4 carries the path only, so a story cannot be built or contract-tested without a default.
read: RWB-P6-E1046-CON sections 11, 12.1 and 12.8; FSD P7 v3 A2.11 AC-P7-011-01 and A2.12 AC-EXC-P7-012-01; WP B2-P7-013 contract dependency RWB-P6-E1046-CON.
confirm: Contract owner of RWB-P6-E1046-CON at the contract review
impact: A renamed parameter or field touches one client, one fake and one section of this story; no business value changes.

text: The merge-field set of a version and the catalog version in force arrive in the answer of the same catalog contract read of ASM-B2-P7-013-4, as the merge codes of the version with the catalog version that carries them, and the body is never fetched: GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/content is named as the owner's operation and not called, because this story stores merge codes and the body reference and no body.
why: The legacy story reads the merge codes of a body and compares them with the catalog, while a separate microservice cannot read the body without a second call; the contract baseline exposes the content operation as a binary and publishes no merge-field element, so the set has to arrive with the version read.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-046 sections 4 and 11 (DF-REF-069 merge_codes, DF-REF-252 to DF-REF-260); RWB-P6-E1046-CON sections 11 and 12.1; FSD P7 v3 A2.11 AC-EXC-P7-011-02.
confirm: Contract owner of RWB-P6-E1046-CON with the rwb-comms catalogue owner
impact: If the set needs its own operation the client makes one more read inside the same 2 s budget; the refusal behaviour is unchanged.

text: The catalog version in force on a business date is the version with the highest valid from on or before that date returned by the catalog contract, and it is the value recorded on the row; the legacy fixture MF-2026.11 stays in force until MF-2026.12 takes effect on 2026-12-15, and no catalog version is held in code, in configuration or in a cache of this service.
why: The legacy rule selects a template version by date (BR2) and the FSD fixes the catalog version as data in force, while no source gives the read path or says whether the catalog version is derived from the merge codes or read on its own; a cached copy would be the second catalogue DP-01 forbids.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-046 BR2, BR4, AC8; FSD P7 v3 A2.12; RWB-P6-E1046-CON section 11 (catalogVersion and validFrom); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01 and DP-11.
confirm: Reference-data owner of rwb-case and the rwb-comms catalogue owner, before SIT
impact: A different derivation changes one comparison and its fixture only; no behaviour and no contract change.

text: The service runs as one login created with the rwb_decision schema by the platform DB work (DP-02); the story names it "the rwb-decision login" until the name is agreed and carries it as a secret reference in the chart, and the row it writes is granted to that login alone with INSERT and SELECT and no UPDATE or DELETE.
why: No source gives the login name and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login, which the target retires, and the append-only rule of BR6 needs the grant to say so.
read: WP B2-P7-013 story line; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 DP-02 and R9; Context pack P7 service row (schema rwb_decision, queue rwb-decision); RWB-P7-E1027-APP section 11.
confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_decision baseline is created
impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

text: The approver named on a version as "LEG-0001" on the legacy load file is stored on the row as a staff reference resolved through the identity mapping of ACE Common, and the row keeps the identifier the catalog answer carries; where the catalog answer carries a uuid the row stores the uuid, and where it carries the file identifier the row stores it unchanged with the source named, so no conversion is invented in this story.
why: The legacy fixtures name the approver as a staff identifier while TSD P7 T3.1 types every user reference as a uuid, and no source states the mapping; recording the value unchanged with its source keeps AC1 assertable without inventing an identity rule.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-046 section 7 background and AC1; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-010 (USER_REF uuid); RWB-P6-E1046-CON section 11 (the approver identifier on a file); FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-011-01.
confirm: Identity owner of ACE Common with the rwb-comms catalogue owner
impact: Low: a resolved uuid instead of the identifier changes one column value and its fixture; no behaviour changes.
